writeup.key_factor: The one play today where the model and the verified context agree on both sides. Utah is without its starting center: Jusuf Nurkic is confirmed OUT (plantar plate tear, weeks) and Tony Bradley is questionable, leaving the Jazz frontcourt thin against Zion Williamson and Yves Missi. New Orleans is healthy — its injury report lists only two-way players. Utah was outrebounded 55-38 in a 123-103 loss at Memphis, while New Orleans put up 120 points in a narrow loss at Indiana. The market has been moving toward New Orleans all day (from +112 this morning to +102 at FanDuel, with Pinnacle already at +100) and the price still pays above our fair line of -128.
writeup.risk: Early-season NBA ratings are still last season's final Elo, so the raw edge is probably overstated — this play rests on the confirmed Nurkic absence and the matchup, not the raw number. New Orleans opens a back-to-back (at Denver tomorrow) and has lost its last 10 games as an underdog (descriptive trend, not a veto). Pass if the price drops below -105, where the edge falls under the 5-point early-season bar.

writeup.key_factor: Showcase Gold that also clears the NHL value gate: a strong Colorado team at home in Denver, priced inside the 1.80-2.20 showcase band at 1.82 (Courtside), with the highest model win probability available inside the band today (59.7%). Colorado scores 4.10 goals per game (second in the league) behind Nathan MacKinnon (16 points), and Mackenzie Blackwood — the regular starter — is the probable goaltender across sources.
writeup.risk: Tampa Bay is the hottest team in this matchup (7-2-0, seven wins in eight, 6-2 at Vegas on Tuesday) with Andrei Vasilevskiy probable in net, and Colorado has lost three of its last five. The NHL rating is still last season's final Elo, and Blackwood is probable rather than officially confirmed — the pregame check re-verifies the crease. Pass if the price drops below -126, where the edge falls under the 4% NHL gate.
